package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions of the malicious lookalike packages)
package_info.why_malicious: A large number of malicious packages were submitted to PyPI with names similar to established dependencies, aiming to trick users into installing them (typosquatting). These packages are designed to compromise the software supply chain by distributing malware.

execution_context.file_location: setup.py or __init__.py of the malicious package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or install-time, the code reads sensitive local files and sends their contents to a remote server via HTTP, enabling data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates local file contents to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access sensitive files or make unsolicited network requests during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated crash reporting or telemetry (with user consent) may send non-sensitive data to a server.
key_indicators: Network requests to untrusted domains during install/import
Obfuscated or minimal code in setup.py or __init__.py

attack_chain.action: User installs a package with a name similar to a popular dependency (typosquatting).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed during installation or import.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, reading sensitive files and sending data to an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data; user system is compromised.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package installation or import
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, SSH keys) by setup.py or __init__.py
Packages with names similar to popular dependencies (typosquatting)
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py containing obfuscated or single-line network/file access code
Unusual or recently registered package names mimicking popular libraries
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with legitimate package maintainers
Connections to known malicious or newly registered domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for network activity during package installation or import, especially to untrusted domains. Scan package files for code that accesses sensitive files or makes network requests. Flag packages with names similar to popular dependencies for manual review.
